metadata.name: Asymmetric bets — investment thesis
metadata.description: Factory graph 2 (D14): triage -> collect fundamentals -> analyze asymmetry -> red team -> size risk -> decide (mandatory human gate, always) -> record and monitoring. One node per step of the D14 sequence; a single final node collects the four ways a crossing can end, so that the process metrics hold per crossing and not only for the approved one.
metadata.source: written by hand from D14 (t116); no synthesis involved

nodes.description: Filters the idea against the investor's criteria before spending research on it, and defines the scope of what to research when it passes.

job.description: the identity of the work itself — `id`, `title` and `body` —, which is where the raw idea arrives: title and hypothesis in free prose

project.description: the static configuration of the class: the investor's triage criteria, the circle of competence they declare and the state of the portfolio (`null` when there is no open position)

asset.description: the thesis's asset; a field of this class, demanded at this node

premise_source.description: where the central premise comes from; a field of this class, demanded at this node

intended_size.description: the intended size for the position, as a % of capital; a field of this class, demanded at this node because without it the risk-ceiling criterion has nothing to judge

outcome.description: passed follows the "advance" edge; failed, the "discard" edge

triaged_thesis.description: the thesis with its research scope defined

checks.instruction: Did every declared criterion get a verdict with evidence from the input itself, and is a "passed" with an unmet criterion justified? Attach, per criterion, the excerpt that supports the verdict.
checks.description: Approving an idea with no floor burns the whole research round that follows — it is this step's expensive defect, and no command detects it.

nodes.description: Gathers the fundamentals from primary documents and separates fact, assumption and gap — explicitly marking every assumption with no source.

triaged_thesis.description: the triaged thesis, with its research scope

fundamentals.description: summary, sourced figures and known risks

assumptions.description: each one with a source or a declared null source

checks.instruction: Does every recorded figure open at the cited source, and is every sourced assumption really supported by it? Attach the quoted excerpt of each source and the list of the assumptions with a null source.
checks.description: An assumption whose source does not support it walks past the red team disguised as a fact — it is the collection's most expensive defect.

nodes.description: Measures the shape of the bet: a limited downside with a traceable floor, a target upside and the scenarios that tie one to the other.

asymmetry.description: downside_max_pct, upside_target_pct, asymmetry_ratio and at least two scenarios

checks.instruction: Does the maximum downside come out of a floor that exists (cash, an asset, a contract) rather than out of an optimistic assumption, and does each scenario fasten itself to assumptions from the list received? Redo the asymmetry-ratio arithmetic and attach it.
checks.description: A narrative floor is the silent way of inflating the asymmetry: the number looks good and the bet turns symmetrical.

nodes.description: A role dedicated to knocking the thesis down with counter-evidence of its own; a thesis that does not answer a serious objection dies here.

fundamentals.description: what the collection gathered — the target, not the proof

outcome.description: passed follows the "survives" edge; failed, the "dead" edge

objections.description: each one with a severity and the thesis's answer, or null when there was no answer

checks.instruction: Is the counter-evidence external to the material received and dated, were the highest-leverage assumptions attacked, and does no "passed" coexist with a high-severity objection left unanswered? Attach every counter-evidence source.
checks.description: A gate verifies with evidence of its own: rereading the analysis and agreeing with it is not a red team.

nodes.description: Converts asymmetry and surviving objections into a position size, an accepted maximum loss and an observable exit trigger.

asymmetry.description: the analysis that survived the red team

project.description: the static configuration of the class; total capital, currency and the portfolio's current exposure

sizing.description: position_size_pct (with a structural ceiling in the skill's schema), the accepted maximum loss, the exit trigger and the horizon

checks.instruction: Was the loss implied by the size recomputed as a % of total capital, did the surviving objections shrink the number, and is the exit trigger observable by a third party? Attach the redone arithmetic.
checks.description: Sizing by conviction instead of by the loss is the one mistake in this graph that cannot be undone afterwards.

nodes.description: The mandatory human gate, always (D14): assembles the dossier and escalates. No session of this node decides a capital allocation — it only transcribes the decision already recorded.

asymmetry.description: the analysis that survived the red team

sizing.description: the proposed size and the exit trigger

perguntas_respondidas.description: the escalation queue, already answered. Empty is legal and is the common case: the session pauses with an input-request instead of deciding.

outcome.description: passed follows the "approved" edge; failed, the "rejected" edge

human_decision.description: question_id and the literal transcription of the founder's answer. Mandatory: it is what makes it structurally impossible to decide an allocation without a human.

checks.instruction: Is there a recorded answer to this thesis's allocation question, is the quoted text a literal transcription of it, and does the outcome correspond to what it says? Attach the question id and the full text of the answer.
checks.description: Escalating here is mandatory by design, not an exceptional resort: the defect to catch is the session that interprets the human answer in the thesis's favour.

nodes.description: The single final node of the four ways of ending: writes down the crossing's process metrics and what to monitor from here on.

sizing.description: the size decided, when there was one

human_decision.description: null on the crossings that never reached the human gate

process_metrics.description: red_team_ran, sourced_assumptions_fraction, human_decision_id and final_outcome. Process, never P&L (D14).

record.description: the summary of the crossing and the monitoring plan

checks.instruction: Was every metric recomputed from the real outputs of this crossing's nodes, and not from self-report? Attach the recomputation of the sourced-assumptions fraction and the closing path cited from the last node's output.
checks.description: It is this metric that the topographer uses to propose a mutation on the graph; an estimated metric poisons the learning of the whole class.

edges.description: The idea has a floor and a trigger: it is worth spending a research round on it (resultado "passed").
The idea did not get past the first filter; it goes straight to the record, and the crossing still produces a metric (resultado "failed").
A single way out: once the material is collected, it is measured.
A single way out: every analysis goes to the red team, including — and especially — the one that looks good.
The thesis answered the serious objections (resultado "passed"); the objections travel on with it and shrink the size.
A serious objection with no answer kills the thesis (resultado "failed"): the cheapest death in the graph.
A single way out: with the risk sized, the decision goes up to the human.
The founder approved (resultado "passed"): position opened, outcome "monitoring".
The founder refused (resultado "failed"): thesis archived with the decision on record.

custom_fields.name: premise_source
custom_fields.description: Where the thesis's central premise comes from: document, figure, date. Demanded at `triage` because that is the gate that decides whether the idea deserves research, and a thesis with no declared source does not get past that point.

custom_fields.name: asset
custom_fields.description: The asset the thesis proposes: ticker, share, contract. Demanded at `triage` for the same reason as `premise_source` — it is the gate that decides whether the idea deserves research, and a thesis with no identified asset has nothing to triage.

custom_fields.name: downside
custom_fields.description: How much is lost if the thesis is wrong, as estimated by whoever proposes it. Informational: the figures that count are those of `analyze-asymmetry`, and this is the guess that exists before it.

custom_fields.name: upside
custom_fields.description: How much is gained if the thesis is right, as estimated by whoever proposes it. Informational for the same reason as `downside`.

custom_fields.name: intended_size
custom_fields.description: The size whoever proposes the thesis is asking for, as a % of capital. Demanded at `triage` because the portfolio's risk-ceiling criterion is judged against it: without the number, the criterion comes out `undetermined` on every crossing, and not for want of data in the world — for want of a field to declare it in (t263).

project.description: The base class's example configuration: these are the criteria, the circle of competence and the portfolio of the reference investor, and it is what lets `triage` dispatch without anybody assembling an input by hand. A project variant overwrites this whole object with the real criteria and the live state of the portfolio of whoever invests (D13) — there is no portfolio-state mechanism in the control plane, so what is here is a still picture, and keeping it current is editing a document.
triage_criteria: the downside is limited by net cash or a real asset, not by a narrative
there is a dated event that forces a repricing within 12 months
the thesis fits inside the declared circle of competence
the intended size fits inside the portfolio's risk ceiling
circle_of_competence: transport infrastructure under long-term contract: ports, terminals and concessions
companies with net cash trading below the value of their assets
dated corporate events: spin-off, asset sale, going private
